```{r}

  df$Date <- ymd_hms(df$Date)   # "2014-09-18 00:00:00+00:00"
  df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date)   
  return(df)
})
```

```{r}
names = names(data_list)
#extract only Close and Volume
data_list <- lapply(names(data_list), function(name) {
  df <- data_list[[name]]
  ticker <- sub("df_", "", name)
  
  df <- df[, c("Date", "Close", "Volume")]
  
  colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "Close"]  <- paste0("Close_", ticker)
  colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "Volume"] <- paste0("Volume_", ticker)
  
  return(df)
})

names(data_list) <- names
```

```{r}
# Moves df_BTC to the front, followed by all other existing items
data_list <- data_list[c("df_BTC", setdiff(names(data_list), "df_BTC"))]
merged_outer <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "Date", all = TRUE), data_list)

close_cols <- grep("^Close_", colnames(merged_outer), value = TRUE)
xts_close <- xts(merged_outer[, close_cols], order.by = merged_outer$Date)
log_returns <- diff(log(xts_close))
```

```{r}

```

\*\*Skewness (asymmetry)\*\* `≈ 0` → symmetric, `> 0` → right-skewed (long right tail, occasional big gains), `< 0` → left-skewed (long left tail, occasional big losses)

\*\*Kurtosis (tail heaviness)\*\* If using regular kurtosis: Normal distribution = 3\
Interpretation:\
High kurtosis → fat tails (extreme events more likely)\
Low kurtosis → thin tails (more “stable”)

```{r}
na_range_date <- function(x, dates) {
  idx <- which(!is.na(x))
  if(length(idx) == 0) return(c(start = as.Date(NA), end = as.Date(NA)))
  c(start = dates[min(idx)], end = dates[max(idx)])
}

asset_period <- sapply(log_ret_df[, -1], na_range_date, dates = log_ret_df$date)

asset_period <- t(asset_period)
asset_period <- data.frame(
  Asset = rownames(asset_period),
  start = as.Date(asset_period[, "start"], origin = "1970-01-01"),
  end   = as.Date(asset_period[, "end"], origin = "1970-01-01"),
  row.names = NULL
)

asset_period
```

# GO-GARCH

Returns→VAR mean→GO-GARCH volatility→ICA factors→GHYP shocks

```{r}
df_filtered <- na.omit(as.matrix(log_returns))
```

```         
gogarchspec(mean.model = list(model = c("constant", "AR", "VAR"), robust = FALSE,  lag = 1, lag.max = NULL, lag.criterion = c("AIC", "HQ", "SC", "FPE"),  external.regressors = NULL,  robust.control = list("gamma" = 0.25, "delta" = 0.01, "nc" = 10, "ns" = 500)),  variance.model = list(model = "sGARCH", garchOrder = c(1,1), submodel = NULL,  variance.targeting = FALSE), distribution.model = c("mvnorm", "manig", "magh"),  ica = c("fastica", "radical"),  ica.fix = list(A = NULL, K = NULL), ...) 
```

```{r}
fits <- vector("list", 54)

for (i in 1:54) {
  set.seed(4595440)
  mean_model = go_garch_conditions$mean_model[i]
  p = go_garch_conditions$p[i]
  q = go_garch_conditions$q[i]
  dist = as.character(go_garch_conditions$dist[i])
  ica = as.character(go_garch_conditions$ica[i])
  
  spec <- gogarchspec(
    mean.model = list(model = mean_model, lag = 1),
    variance.model = list(model = "sGARCH", garchOrder = c(p,q)),
    distribution.model = dist,
    ica = ica
    )

  tryCatch({  
    fits[[i]] <- gogarchfit(spec, data = df_filtered)
  
  }, error = function(e){
    fits[[i]] <<-NA
  })
  
}

names(fits) <- paste0("fit", 1:54)
```

```{r}
#log-likelihood values
ll_values <- sapply(fits, function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || !inherits(x, "goGARCHfit")) {
    return(NA)
  } else {
    return(as.numeric(likelihood(x)))
  }
})

#AIC values
AIC_values <- sapply(fits, function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || !inherits(x, "goGARCHfit")) {
    return(NA)
  } else {
    ll <- likelihood(x)
    k  <- length(coef(x))
    AIC <- -2*ll + 2*k
    return(as.numeric(AIC))
  }
})

go_garch_conditions$ll = ll_values
go_garch_conditions$AIC = AIC_values
```

Ljung-Box test results on the standardized residual

```{r}
ljung_box_test <- function(fit, X, lag = 20){

  W <- fit@mfit$W
  
  # latent factors
  F <- X %*% t(W)
  
  # conditional sigma of factors
  sigma_f <- fit@mfit$factor.sigmas
  
  # standardized innovations
  Z <- F / sigma_f
  
  # p-values for each factor
  p_raw <- apply(Z, 2, function(x){
    Box.test(x, lag = lag, type = "Ljung")$p.value
  })
  
  p_squared <- apply(Z^2, 2, function(x){
    Box.test(x, lag = lag, type = "Ljung")$p.value
  })
  
  return(list(
    raw = p_raw,
    squared = p_squared
  ))
}
```

```{r}
LB_results <- lapply(fits, function(x){

  if (!inherits(x,"goGARCHfit")){
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  ljung_box_test(x, df_filtered)

})
```

```{r}
LB_raw_count <- sapply(LB_results, function(x){

  if(is.null(x)) return(NA)

  sum(x$raw > 0.05)

})


LB_squared_count <- sapply(LB_results, function(x){

  if(is.null(x)) return(NA)

  sum(x$squared > 0.05)

})
```


## Interpretation

A grid search over 54 GO-GARCH specifications was conducted, varying the GARCH orders, mean specifications, ICA algorithms, and conditional distributions. The model with the lowest AIC corresponds to a specification with a constant mean, RADICAL ICA, and a multivariate generalized hyperbolic (MAGH) distribution.

Models incorporating AR mean dynamics frequently failed to converge, suggesting that linear predictability in the conditional mean is not supported by the data. In contrast, the constant mean specification yielded stable and consistently superior fits across all distributional assumptions. The results further indicate that RADICAL ICA provides a more robust factor decomposition than FastICA in this empirical setting, while heavy-tailed distributions such as MAGH substantially improve model fit relative to the Gaussian specification.

1.  **GARCH order: no significance effect**

    cannot observe any big differences among (1,1), (1,2), and (2,1)

2.  \*\*Mean Model\*\* using "constant" shows higher LL values than the model with "VAR"\
    We are having 10 crypto assets in one model, so mean value of returns can not be easily predicted.\
    This might be the reason why the mean model with constant structure shows better performance.

3.  **Algorithm for ICA**

    There are two options in this parameter,\

    - Fast Fixed Point ICA (**fastica**): Find non-normal signals quickly

    \- The Robust Auccurate and Direct ICA algorithm (**radical**): Carefully minimize dependence, even if slower\
    \
    =\> with ICA: radical \> fastica (radical is better than fastica) =\>?

4.  **Go Distributions**

    -Multivariate normal(mvnorm): symmetric, this tails

    -Multivariate Affine NIG (manig): Heavy tails, skweness

    -GHYP distributions of Schmidt(magh): very felxible, Inclues several distributions as special cases (Including ING), most powerful but also easiest to overfit.

    =\>"magh" has better than other ones.

    Our dataset needs models with a structure that can capture the heavy tails

Among the candidate mean specifications (constant, AR(1), and VAR(1)), the constant mean model was ultimately selected. This result is consistent with the autocorrelation analysis presented in Section X, which indicated little evidence of serial dependence in cryptocurrency returns

## Vine Copula

Vine copula is a hierarchical construction of high-dimensional dependence using a sequence of bivariate copulas arranged in a tree structure.

**C-vine:** one main asset (e.g. BTC), star structure

**D-vineGG:** chain structure (BTC → ETH → ADA → ...)

**R-vine (general) :** full flexible network

| family  | meaning                   |
|---------|---------------------------|
| t       | symmetric tail dependence |
| clayton | lower tail (crash)        |
| gumbel  | upper tail (boom)         |
| tawn    | asymmetric tail           |
| bb8     | nonlinear flexible        |
| frank   | weak dependence           |
| indep   | no dependence             |

```{r}
vine_fit <- RVineStructureSelect(u_uni)
```

```{r}
rvine_matrix = vine_fit$Matrix
rvine_matrix
```

vinefit\$Matrix shows

- Which variables are dependence hub

- How the conditional tree formed

- It gives us information about how could we interpret tau values from tau matrix. For example, if we see the tau value 0.8146 (located at [10, 4]-\> which means it represents a pair between variable 7 and 5 (since the first appeared value in the 4th column is 7 in the Matrix,, and the value in the 10th row in the 4th column is "5". So, the value in [10,4] is representing asset number 7 and 5.


**vine_fit\$tau** contains the estimated **Kendall's tau values** for the pair-copulas in the vine structure**.**

**Kendall's tau:** a rank based measure of dependence strength between two variables.

Unlike Pearson correlation, it captures:

- nonlinear dependence

- monotonic relationships

- dependence implied by copulas

  and kendall's tau is more robust to outliers and heavy tails.

| Tau value | Meaning             |
|-----------|---------------------|
| 0         | independence        |
| 0.1–0.3   | weak dependence     |
| 0.3–0.6   | moderate dependence |
| 0.6+      | strong dependence   |
| negative  | inverse dependence  |

```{r}
extract_vine_table <- function(vine_fit) {
  d <- ncol(vine_fit$Matrix)
  mat <- vine_fit$Matrix
  fam_mat <- vine_fit$family
  tau_mat <- round(vine_fit$tau, 4)
  
  result <- list()
  
  # Loop over trees (Tree 1 corresponds to bottom row d of the matrices)
  for (t in 1:(d - 1)) {
    row_idx <- d - t + 1
    
    for (col_idx in 1:(d - t)) {
      # Node 1 is the element at row_idx, col_idx
      v1 <- mat[row_idx, col_idx]
      # Node 2 is the diagonal element for that column
      v2 <- mat[col_idx, col_idx]
      
      # Extract conditioning set (elements in matrix above row_idx in that column)
      if (row_idx < d) {
        cond_set <- mat[(row_idx + 1):d, col_idx]
        cond_str <- paste(sort(cond_set), collapse = ",")
        edge_label <- paste0(v1, ",", v2, " | ", cond_str)
      } else {
        edge_label <- paste0(v1, ",", v2)
      }
      
      fam_code <- fam_mat[row_idx, col_idx]
      fam_name <- BiCopName(fam_code, short = FALSE)
      tau_val <- tau_mat[row_idx, col_idx]
      
      result[[length(result) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        Tree = t,
        Edge = edge_label,
        Family_Code = fam_code,
        Family_Name = fam_name,
        Kendall_Tau = tau_val,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  }
  
  do.call(rbind, result)
}

# Generate the summary table
vine_summary_df <- extract_vine_table(vine_fit)

# View the full table or just Tree 1
head(vine_summary_df, 9)
```

```{r}
# 1. Define portfolio weights
w <- rep(1/10, 10)

# 2. Create list of returns datasets
data_list <- list(
  "Observed"   = exp(df_filtered) - 1,
  "GO-GARCH"   = exp(x_sim_gogarch) - 1,
    "gogarch+vc"     = exp(x_sim_ar[(burn_in + 1):nrow(x_sim_ar), ])-1
  ) #exp(sim_results$x_sim) - 

# 3. Define function to compute VaR and ES
calc_risk_metrics <- function(ret_matrix, weights) {
  # Calculate portfolio return series
  port_ret <- as.vector(as.matrix(ret_matrix) %*% weights)
  
  # Compute quantiles at 5% and 1% levels
  q95 <- unname(quantile(port_ret, 0.05))
  q99 <- unname(quantile(port_ret, 0.01))
  
  # Compute VaR & ES (expressed as positive loss values)
  data.frame(
    VaR_95 = -q95,
    VaR_99 = -q99,
    ES_95  = -mean(port_ret[port_ret <= q95]),
    ES_99  = -mean(port_ret[port_ret <= q99])
  )
}

# 4. Apply metric function across datasets and row-bind into summary table
results_list <- lapply(data_list, calc_risk_metrics, weights = w)
results_df <- do.call(rbind, results_list)

# Display final table
print(results_df)
```

### gogarch_optim

```{r}
gogarch_optim = function(go_garch_conditions, df){
  k <- nrow(go_garch_conditions)
  fits <- vector("list", k)

  for (i in 1:k) {
    set.seed(4595440)
    mean_model = go_garch_conditions$mean_model[i]
    p = go_garch_conditions$p[i]
    q = go_garch_conditions$q[i]
    dist = as.character(go_garch_conditions$dist[i])
    ica = as.character(go_garch_conditions$ica[i])
    
    spec <- gogarchspec(
      mean.model = list(model = mean_model, lag = 1),
      variance.model = list(model = "sGARCH", garchOrder = c(p,q)),
      distribution.model = dist,
      ica = ica
      )
  
    tryCatch({  
      fits[[i]] <- gogarchfit(spec, data = df)
    
    }, error = function(e){
      fits[[i]] <<-NA
    })
    
  }
  
  names(fits) <- paste0("fit", 1:k)
  
  ll_values <- sapply(fits, function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || !inherits(x, "goGARCHfit")) {
    return(NA)
    } else {
    return(as.numeric(likelihood(x)))
    }
  })

  #AIC values
  AIC_values <- sapply(fits, function(x) {
    if (is.null(x) || !inherits(x, "goGARCHfit")) {
      return(NA)
    } else {
      ll <- likelihood(x)
      k  <- length(coef(x))
      AIC <- -2*ll + 2*k
      return(as.numeric(AIC))
    }
  })

  go_garch_conditions$ll <- ll_values
  go_garch_conditions$AIC <- AIC_values
  
  LB_results <- lapply(fits, function(x){
  if (!inherits(x,"goGARCHfit")){
    return(NULL)
  }
  ljung_box_test(x, df)
  })
  
  go_garch_conditions$LB_raw_pass <- sapply(LB_results, function(x){
    if(is.null(x)) return(NA)
    sum(x$raw > 0.05)
  })
  
  go_garch_conditions$LB_squared_pass <- sapply(LB_results, function(x){
    if(is.null(x)) return(NA)
    sum(x$squared > 0.05)
  })
  
  valid_idx <- which(!is.na(AIC_values))
  sorted_idx <- valid_idx[order(AIC_values[valid_idx], decreasing = FALSE)]
  top10 <- sorted_idx[1:10]
  results_top10 = go_garch_conditions[top10,]
 
  return(list(
    result = go_garch_conditions,
    result_top10 = results_top10,
    fits = fits
  ))
}
```

### Lijung-Box test result

```{r}
lb_test <- function(fitted_model, df){
  

  best_model = fitted_model
  R <- as.matrix(df)
  X <- R - best_model@mfit$mu
  W <- best_model@mfit$W
  F <- X %*% t(W)

  # conditional sigma of factors
  sigma_f <- best_model@mfit$factor.sigmas 

  # standardized innovations
  Z <- F / sigma_f
  
  lb_results <- data.frame(
    Factor = integer(),
    LB_raw = numeric(),
    p_raw = numeric(),
    LB_squared = numeric(),
    p_squared = numeric()
  )

  for(i in 1:ncol(Z)){
  
    raw_test <- Box.test(
      Z[, i],
      lag = 20,
      type = "Ljung-Box"
    )
    
    sq_test <- Box.test(
      Z[, i]^2,
      lag = 20,
      type = "Ljung-Box"
    )
    
    lb_results <- rbind(
      lb_results,
      data.frame(
        Factor = i,
        LB_raw = raw_test$statistic,
        p_raw = raw_test$p.value,
        LB_squared = sq_test$statistic,
        p_squared = sq_test$p.value
      )
    )
  }
  
  return(lb_results)
  
}
```

### Simulation

```{r}
#only  AR mean model + GARCH(1,1) for now...
ggvc_sim <- function(fitted_model, df, burn_in = 1e4, N = 2e4) {
  
  best_model <- fitted_model
  R <- as.matrix(df)
  
  # 1. GO-GARCH
  X <- R - best_model@mfit$mu
  W <- best_model@mfit$W
  F_factor <- X %*% t(W)
  sigma_f  <- best_model@mfit$factor.sigmas 
  Z        <- F_factor / sigma_f
  
  # 2. Vine Copula
  u_uni    <- as.matrix(pobs(Z))
  vine_fit <- RVineStructureSelect(u_uni)  
  
  set.seed(4595440)
  u_sim <- RVineSim(N, vine_fit)

  # Quantile
  z_sim <- sapply(1:ncol(u_sim), function(k) {
    quantile(Z[, k], probs = u_sim[, k], type = 8)
  })  

  # 3.  GARCH simulation
  m <- ncol(z_sim)
  
  sigma_sim <- matrix(NA, nrow = N, ncol = m)
  f_sim     <- matrix(NA, nrow = N, ncol = m)
  
  omega = coef(best_model)["omega", ]
  alpha1 = coef(best_model)["alpha1", ]
  beta1 = coef(best_model)["beta1", ]
  
  sigma_0 = sqrt(omega/(1-alpha1 - beta1))   
  f_0 = sigma_0 * z_sim[1,]
  
  
  sigma_sim[1, ] <- sigma_0
  f_sim[1, ] <- f_0
  
  for(i in 2:nrow(z_sim)){
  
    sigma_square <-
      omega +
      alpha1 * f_sim[i-1, ]^2 +
      beta1  * sigma_sim[i-1, ]^2
  
    sigma_sim[i, ] <- sqrt(sigma_square)
  
    f_sim[i, ] <- sigma_sim[i, ] * z_sim[i, ]
  }
  

  # 4. Mixing Matrix A
  A <- best_model@mfit$A
  eps_sim <- f_sim %*% t(A)

  # 5. Flexible AR/Mean Structure
  ar_coefs <- best_model@mfit$arcoef
  mu_vec   <- ar_coefs["mu", ]
  
  # AR(1) 
  has_ar1  <- "ar1" %in% rownames(ar_coefs)
  phi_vec  <- if(has_ar1) ar_coefs["ar1", ] else rep(0, ncol(df))

  x_sim_ar <- matrix(NA, nrow = N, ncol = ncol(df))
  
  #initial value
  x_sim_ar[1, ] <- (1 - phi_vec) * mu_vec + eps_sim[1, ]

  # AR(1) 
  for (t in 2:N) {
    x_sim_ar[t, ] <- (1 - phi_vec) * mu_vec +
                     phi_vec * x_sim_ar[t - 1, ] +
                     eps_sim[t, ]
  }
  
  sim_model <- gogarchsim(best_model, 
                        startMethod="unconditional", 
                        n.sim=2e4, n.start=0, m.sim=1,
                        presigma = matrix(sigma_0, ncol = 1),
                        rseed = 4595440)

  x_sim_gogarch <- sim_model@msim$seriesSim[[1]][10001:20000, ]


  return(list(
    x_sim     = x_sim_ar[10001:20000, ],
    sigma_sim = sigma_sim,    
    f_sim     = f_sim,        
    vine_fit  = vine_fit,
    x_sim_gogarch = x_sim_gogarch,
    gogarchsim_model = sim_model

  ))
}

```

### Correlation Matrix

```{r}
cor_function = function(x_sim, x_raw){
  
  cor_Xsim = cor(x_sim, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  cor_Xraw = cor(x_raw, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  
  mse = mean((cor_Xsim[upper.tri(cor_Xsim)] - cor_Xraw[upper.tri(cor_Xraw)])^2)
  mae = mean(abs(cor_Xsim[upper.tri(cor_Xsim)] - cor_Xraw[upper.tri(cor_Xraw)]))
  return(list(
    rmse = sqrt(mse),
    mae = mae,
    cor_Xsim = cor_Xsim,
    cor_Xraw = cor_Xraw
  ))
  
}
```

```{r}
period_analysis <- function(df, conditions) {
  
  # 1. GO-GARCH fitting
  go_optim <- gogarch_optim(conditions, df)
  
  fit <- go_optim$fits[[1]]
  
  # 2. Ljung-Box test
  lb <- lb_test(fit, df)
  
  # 3. Simulation
  sim_results <- ggvc_sim(fit, df)
  
  # 4. Correlation comparison
  cor_gogarch <- cor_function(
    sim_results$x_sim_gogarch,
    df
  )
  
  cor_vine <- cor_function(
    sim_results$x_sim,
    df
  )
  
  return(list(
    optim = go_optim,
    fit = fit,
    lb_test = lb,
    simulation = sim_results,
    cor_gogarch = cor_gogarch,
    cor_vine = cor_vine
  ))
}
```

```{r}
for (period in names(df_list)) {
  
  df <- df_list[[period]]
  sim <- sim_list[[period]]
  
  # 1. Raw data
  cor_raw <- cor(df, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  
  corrplot_save(
    filename = paste0("corr_", period, "_raw"),
    cor_matrix = cor_raw
  )
  
  
  # 2. GO-GARCH
  cor_gogarch <- cor(sim$x_sim_gogarch,use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

  corrplot_save(
    filename = paste0("corr_", period, "_gogarch"),
    cor_matrix = cor_gogarch
  )
  
  
  # 3. Vine + GO-GARCH
  cor_vine <- cor(sim$x_sim, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  
  corrplot_save(
    filename = paste0("corr_", period, "_vine"),
    cor_matrix = cor_vine
  )
}
```
